overview: This file consists of three cross-reference sheets concerning Japan’s acquisition, processing, and military use of tin between April 1940 and March 1942. The referenced documents sought information about tin smelters in Japan amid conflicting reports from Bolivia, investigated the suspected diversion to Japan of tin ostensibly shipped to New York aboard Japanese vessels, and transmitted a report on the relationship between tin acquisition and Japanese aircraft production. Although the underlying papers are filed elsewhere, the sheets reveal State Department interest in Japan’s strategic access to tin before and during the Pacific War.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on tin smelters in Japan
subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a despatch requesting information about tin smelters in Japan because reports received in Bolivia were conflicting.
subfiles.summary: The sheet refers researchers to despatch no. 181, dated April 3, 1940, from Bolivia and associated with Jenkins. The referenced paper sought clarification about the existence or operation of tin smelters in Japan, a subject on which reports in Bolivia conflicted. The original was filed under number 894.24/889.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on suspected diversion of tin shipments to Japan
subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a telegram requesting data on tin arriving in New York aboard Japanese vessels amid suspicion that shipments were being diverted to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The sheet records concern that tin carried by Japanese vessels and nominally shipped to New York might instead be diverted to Japan. It references a December 5, 1940 telegram to Singapore, associated with Patton, requesting monthly figures for tin arrivals in New York on Japanese ships. The original telegram was filed under number 811.6354/735.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on tin acquisition and Japanese aircraft production
subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a letter submitting a report on the relationship between Japanese tin acquisition and aircraft production.
subfiles.summary: The sheet points to a March 26, 1942 letter from the Coordinator of Information. That letter submitted a report entitled “The Relation of Tin Acquisition to Airplane Production in Japan.” The original was filed under number 894.248/47, linking raw-material intelligence to assessment of Japan’s wartime aviation capacity.

interest: The file is useful because it connects three stages of strategic-resource intelligence: Japan’s domestic smelting capacity, the possible covert diversion of overseas tin shipments, and the metal’s importance to aircraft production. The December 1940 sheet is especially suggestive of efforts to reconstruct clandestine trade through vessel and port-arrival statistics. Together, the cross-references also guide researchers to related documents filed under different decimal classifications, illustrating how information about strategic commodities was dispersed within State Department records.
